items.title: Koti Deepotsavam emerges as grand confluence of Shaiva, Vaishnava traditions in Telangana
points: Koti Deepotsavam offers devotees an opportunity to perform abhishekams, offer bilva leaves to Shiva Lingams, worship the Goddess and participate in special pujas and other ceremonies.

A confluence of Shaiva and Vaishnava traditions, a congregation of revered spiritual heads from across the country and the illumination of a crore lamps have made Koti Deepotsavam one of Telangana’s biggest religious celebrations outside temple premises.
Over the past 13 years, Koti Deepotsavam has given a distinctive identity to the month of Kartika and to Telangana.
The initiative began in 2012 as a Laksha Deepotsavam, or the lighting of one lakh lamps, and the following year evolved into Koti Deepotsavam, involving a crore lamps.

The genesis of the initiative lay in a visit by Sringeri Dakshinamnaya Peetham Jagadguru Sri Bharati Tirtha Mahaswami to Hyderabad during his Vijaya Yatra in 2012, when Kartika Deepotsavam was combined with the darshan of the Jagadguru for the Guru Vandanam.
By 2013, the Laksha Deepotsavam had grown into Koti Deepotsavam.

items.title: PM Modi opens SCO event in Pakistan minister Malik’s presence
points: Cultural connections are the strongest guarantee of global peace, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Friday as he opened a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting in Delhi in the presence of leaders from 10 member countries, including Pakistan.

Pakistan climate change minister Musadik Masood Malik – who is leading the country’s delegation at the first SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum – is the first Pakistani leader to visit India in more than three years.
He is also the first Pakistani minister to travel to India since the four-day conflict between the two sides in May 2025.
The Congress hit out at the government, saying it should be ashamed to invite a Pakistani minister but the Bharatiya Janata Party rejected the allegations.

Malik, a member of the ruling PML-N party, was among the Pakistani leaders who reacted strongly to India’s decision to suspend the Indus Waters Treaty as part of a package of punitive diplomatic and economic measures.
Pakistan is the chair of the SCO Council of Heads of State for 2026-27.

items.title: Shimla’s iconic Peterhoff Hotel mired in political controversy over its future
points: Perched on Shimla’s tranquil Chaura Maidan enclave, Hotel Peterhoff has witnessed history unfolding across the arc of India’s journey, from a British colony to an independent nation.
Commissioned in 1863 as the summer seat of the British Raj, the estate housed seven consecutive Viceroys at the zenith of imperial power.
Between 1948 and 1949, its courtroom was the focus of a grieving nation during the trial of Nathuram Godse and his co-conspirators for the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi.
In 1971, the estate transitioned into Himachal Pradesh’s Raj Bhavan upon the hill state’s attainment of full statehood.
The union said that 70 to 80% of the hotel can be restored to a functional state and upgraded with modern amenities.
In 1971, when Himachal Pradesh became a full-fledged state, Peterhoff was the Raj Bhavan, the official residence of the governor.
The then BJP government led by Shanta Kumar in 1990 renamed the building Meghdoot.It also decided to develop it as a five-star hotel, which was built in 1991.

items.title: In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare
points: In Attappady, a predominantly tribal area of Palakkad district in Keralam, a mother soothes her baby. | Photo Credit: Sakeer Hussain Between the pages of a logbook recording Dakshina’s treatment are ₹100, ₹50, ₹20, and ₹10 notes.
Dakshina’s mother, Minnal Rani, had filed them away for her daughter’s medical expenses.
The child is gone, but the money remains untouched.
Born on June 13, 2025, she was taken to many hospitals, including one in Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam’s capital.
Rani and her husband Chandra Sekhar say the hospital refused to release their daughter’s body until they paid a bill of ₹10,000.
Dakshina’s death is among a series of 10 infant deaths reported this year from Attappadi, a predominantly tribal settlement.
Of the 10 infant deaths, six involved congenital anomalies, with heart defects among the commonly reported conditions.

items.title: Gold Logs Worst Week Since March on Hawkish Fed, AI Selloff
points: (Bloomberg) -- Gold slid for a fifth day — notching its biggest weekly decline since March — as a hawkish Federal Reserve signaled more interest-rate hikes and a rout in AI stocks spurred selling across metals markets.
Bullion tumbled, trading near $3,500 an ounce Friday, and lost nearly 9% this week, after hitting its lowest level since September 2025.
Silver has fallen over 15% in the past five sessions.
The sharp rout in gold has decisively broken below $4,000 an ounce, a level some investors believed would provide a floor for bullion, with support from central-bank purchases and other dip-buyers.
The prospect of tighter monetary policy has kept Treasury yields elevated, with 10-year borrowing costs hovering around 5%.

Globally, investors are betting that major central banks, including the Fed, the European Central Bank and the Bank of England, will keep rates largely unchanged for years once they’ve finished hiking at the end of 2027.
Spot gold fell 2.4% to $3,538.49 an ounce.

items.title: Baltic Dry Index Eases For 2nd Day
points: The Baltic Exchange’s dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, was down for a second session on Friday, falling by 0.1% to 2,898 points.

items.title: Russian Vessels Have Shifted From Europe’s Cables to Its Energy Grid
points: Between late August and mid-November, Russia-linked loitering events in that record shifted decisively toward energy.
In the nine days to November 12, it was every loitering event.
In the window to October 6, seven of eight Russia-linked loitering events were telecom-only.
The turn came in the October 21 to November 3 window, when three of seven events were energy, two of them over the BBL interconnector and one over Norpipe.
The Vessels Changed Alongside the Targets Earlier loitering over energy infrastructure mostly involved third-party flagged vessels trading with Russia.
Ships at Poland’s B8 platform, on the FLAGS and Alwyn-Frigg systems, and on BBL.
Two tugs, three small cargo ships, and one vessel under U.S. sanctions for Russian Ministry of Defence logistics work.Through September That is a different population.
Four Vessels Shared a Route and a Behavior Four of the six were sailing from the Black Sea to Murmansk or St. Petersburg.

items.title: Fujairah fuel oil stocks edge up 1% in November so far
points: Fujairah’s fuel oil stocks have averaged 1% higher so far in November than across October, Fujairah Oil Industry Zone (FOIZ) and S&P Global data shows.
Kuwait accounted for 33% of the imports, followed by Iraq (29%) and Nigeria (12%).
Fuel oil exports rose to 474,000 b/d from 279,000 b/d in October, according to cargo tracker Vortexa.
Singapore accounted for 33% of the exports, followed by China (22%) and Turkey (9%).
Exports exceeded imports by 403,000 b/d, making Fujairah a net exporter.
Middle distillate stocks averaged 2.73 million bbls so far in November, up 15% from 2.37 million bbls in October.
Availability in Fujairah has improved this week, despite continued disruption to vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz amid US-Iran tensions.
Source: By Tuhin Roy, ENGINE, https://www.engine.online/news/

In order to promote the spread and development of innovative technologies, ClassNK has offered Innovation Endorsement for Products & Solutions.

items.title: Crew Teams Are Told To Book Flights Early, Yet Nearly Half Of Maritime Crew Tickets Booked A Week Ahead Are Cancelled
points: On the C Teleport platform, maritime crew teams cancelled 48.5% of the tickets they booked a week or more before departure, against 18.1% of tickets booked in the last 24 hours.
For aircrew teams the gap was wider still: 43.5% against 8.6%.

The figures come from two new reports, What are last-minute crew bookings costing your team?, one for maritime and one for aircrew, built on 12 months of crew flight bookings on the C Teleport crew travel platform.
Maritime crew teams booked 63% of crew flights in the final week before departure, and nearly 1 in 4 within 48 hours.
Aircrew teams booked later still: 78.3% in the final week and 24.8% in the last 24 hours, against 11.3% across all industries on the platform.
In aviation, a schedule change, an AOG or a crew member calling in sick changes the roster in its last few days, and 45.7% of aircrew cancellations happen in the 48 hours before departure.

items.title: Transgender persons to be roped in for tax collection in West Bengal
points: The West Bengal government will engage transgender persons to collect municipal tax and spread traffic awareness.
Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Minister Agnimitra Paul said the initiative, called “Brihannala Brigade”, will provide an opportunity for a dignified livelihood for the transpersons.
“The CM wishes that they (transgender people no) longer have to resort to begging at traffic signals; instead, we want to offer them an alternative, respectable livelihood.
Their role will be to sensitise the public about traffic rules and safety measures,” Ms. Paul said on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
According to Kolkata Municipal Corporation estimates, they have around ₹6800 crore outstanding property tax pending, including personal properties, mixed-use properties, and commercial properties.
In 2022, the previous Mamata Banerjee government decided to allow transgender persons to apply for government jobs under the general category to help them have better opportunities in employment.
A Transgender Development Board was set up in 2017, but the board could not undertake many activities for the welfare of members of the community.

The BJP leaders denied allegations of the assault but claimed that Trinamool supporters were trying to incite tensions by gathering outside the police station.

“@BJP4Bengal workers gathered outside Girish Park Police Station today, seemingly intent on harassing, heckling and assaulting our workers, did not even spare ordinary citizens and parents who had come to pick up their children from school,” the party…

items.title: GTA 6 Sales Number Hits a Staggering 30 Million+ Copies, Generating 3.79 Billion in Revenue
points: Take-Two Interactive has revealed GTA 6‘s launch-day sales number in an official post.
According to the official Take-Two report, GTA 6 has already sold over 32.5 million copies and generated over $3.79 billion in revenue by launch day.
This is an unprecedented record no other game has ever met, or is expected to meet in the near future.
The record was previously held by The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998), considered one of the best games of all time.
Although everyone expected GTA 6 to be a massive success, the previous estimated numbers don’t even come close to Take-Two’s official announcement.
Previous estimates assumed GTA 6 would reach around $2.36 billion in revenue, which is almost $1 billion short of the actual number at launch.
With GTA 6 yet to come to PC, expect the game to cross GTA 5’s lifetime sales number, 235 million, by a huge margin very soon.

items.title: Chandel district official issues advisory after spurious liquor kills 11 in Manipur
points: The public advisory followed the death of 11 people due to consumption of spurious liquor in the district’s Chakpikarong Sub-Division.
The deaths have been reported since Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
According to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office, 180 others are undergoing treatment at two private hospitals in Imphal.
Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited these hospitals on Friday and took stock of the treatment being provided to the patients.
Advising the general public to exercise utmost caution, the district administration said the cause of the deaths was yet to be “medically and scientifically established”.
The Manipur government partially lifted 30 years of alcohol prohibition in December 2023, although extremist groups in the State continue to target liquor businesses.
Spurious liquor has claimed lives in other northeastern States where prohibition is enforced.
For instance, 23 people were killed in Nagaland’s Mokokchung and Tuensang districts about two months ago.

items.title: Asset-Backed Debt Sales Top Post-GFC Record on AI Strength
points: (Bloomberg) -- Sales of asset-backed securities have surpassed their highest level since the Great Financial Crisis for a third straight year, as builders of artificial intelligence infrastructure continue to tap markets for financing and cash-rich…

This week the sales of bonds — backed by assets including data center leases, auto loans and gym memberships — have surpassed $380 billion so far this year, topping issuance of more than $367 billion for all of 2025, Bloomberg-compiled data show.
Securitizations tied to AI infrastructure helped to push overall issuance above the 2025 level despite a slight dip in automobile-linked transactions, which make up almost half of sales.

“The same could be said for aviation finance, which saw aircraft ABS take a much bigger share of the debt financing pie in 2026.” Data center and fiber infrastructure sales total $28.6 billion this year, compared with $27.7 billion for the whole of 2025…
Sales of aircraft-linked debt rose to $13.7 billion from $10.3 billion.

items.title: Patna High Court quashes dismissal of teachers and staff of Sanskrit Colleges
points: Principals, teachers, and non-teaching staff of various Sanskrit colleges affiliated with Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (KSDSU) received relief from the Patna High Court on Friday (November 20, 2026).
A single-judge bench presided over by Justice Kumar Manish, while hearing 12 connected petitions (lead case: Birendra Prasad Thakur v.
State of Bihar, CWJC No. 13475/2022), quashed all dismissal orders issued by the Director of Higher Education and the university.

Despite the university’s Syndicate confirming their services, the Director of Higher Education cited the absence of prior approval from the State Government, as required under Section 35(2) of the Bihar State Universities Act, 1976, and rejected these…
In its judgment, the High Court cited the ruling of a Full Bench in Braj Kishore Singh v.
“Dismissing an employee on technical grounds after more than a decade of service constitutes a violation of Articles 14, 16, and 21 of the Constitution,” the court observed.

items.title: Cabinet decision to forfeit Basava Mantapa book yet to take effect for want of notification
points: The controversial book Basava Mantapa. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement A day after the State Cabinet decided to forfeit all copies of the controversial book Basava Mantapa, it was still available in bookstores on Friday, and in fact, the demand had…
The Cabinet decision is yet to be implemented for want of a notification from the State government.

Shivakumar on Friday said that his government will “not tolerate derogatory remarks against Basavanna, the cultural leader of the State” and had instructed officials to forfeit all copies of the book.

Parameshwara, briefing the media after Thursday’s Cabinet meeting, had said they were not banning the book but “forfeiting all copies”, and there was a provision for the same under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023.
Section 98 of BNSS, 2023, provides the State government with this power.
However, the police can move to forfeit copies of the book only after the State government issues a notification under Section 98 of BNSS, 2023.

items.title: Mahipalpur flyover a daily traffic bottleneck for city commuters
points: Gajender Rawat, a private-sector employee who travels from his residence in Paschim Vihar to Gurugram for work, said he spends at least 30-40 minutes crossing the flyover every day.
“Vehicles begin slowing down almost as soon as we enter the flyover while travelling from Delhi towards Gurugram, with congestion stretching towards the Gurugram side.
On Wednesday, he took over 1.5 hours to cross the stretch during peak hours.

Commuters have also repeatedly flagged the problem on social media, describing the flyover as a “permanent choke point” and raising concerns over traffic management and passenger pick-ups and drop-offs along the stretch.
“Over the last five-six months, there has been a permanent traffic jam at Mahipalpur flyover.
Cabs drop passengers near the hotel at Mahipalpur flyover,” a commuter wrote on X, sharing a Google Maps screenshot showing a travel time of 1 hour and 43 minutes for 36 km.

items.title: Iran War Oil Premium Evaporates as Global Crude Supplies Surge
points: By Nathan Risser and Yongchang Chin (Bloomberg) –The price of US sour oil has plunged, as a surge in crude supply from Venezuela, Canada and the Middle East gives refiners ample barrels to choose from.
Mars has dropped from a $10 premium to a $4 discount to WTI futures in less than a month.
US refiners, major buyers of heavier oil along the Gulf Coast and in the Midwest, have benefited from increased supplies from Canada and Latin America.

“Incremental supply looks to be dominated by heavier and more sour barrels, especially out of Canada, Venezuela, and the Middle East,” Valero’s head of crude supply Randy Hawkins said in an October earnings call.
It’s a “race to the bottom” Phillips 66’s executive vice president of marketing and commercial Brian Mandell said on a call with analysts the same month.

items.title: Comments by Abhishek Banerjee painful but not contemptuous: Calcutta High Court
points: The Calcutta High Court, on Friday (November 20, 2026), while extending interim protection to Diamond Harbour MP and Trinamool leader Abhishek Banerjee in a case filed by the police, said that the comments made by the Trinamool leader were painful and…

Justice Saugata Bhattacharya of the Calcutta High Court was responding to comments made by Additional Advocate General Rajdeep Mazumder, who informed the Court during the hearing that Mr. Banerjee had posted tweets in which he made derogatory remarks about…
“The Court finds these comments are not wilful, deliberate and contumacious contempt, though the comments are painful.
Why is he harming his position?” Justice Bhattacharya said.
The Court extended interim protection in a case filed by the police, accusing the MP of making provocative speech during the run-up to the 2026 Assembly polls.
Mr. Banerjee had moved the High Court, demanding that the FIR against him be quashed.
The development comes days after Justice Krishna Rao of the Calcutta High Court issued criminal contempt proceedings against Abhishek Banerjee.

items.title: First phase of bird flu containment completed in Alappuzha
points: A total of four Rapid Response Teams led the disinfection activities, which were carried out in accordance with protocol at the locations where the birds had been culled and incinerated.
The area was disinfected using flame treatment, sodium hypochlorite spraying and lime spreading.
With this, the first phase of bird flu containment has been completed, according to an official communication.

The authorities said that samples would be collected from the 10-kilometre surveillance zone around the epicentres and sent to the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal once every two weeks.
The area would be declared free of bird flu only if the samples tested negative over a period of three months.

Kaloor, Vyttila, Edappally, Jos Junction, and Thripunithura are among the selected junctions.

Minor changes, such as adding pedestrian crossings, installing lights and removing boards or other obstructions that block visibility, will be introduced to ease traffic, Ms. Nishanthini told a meet-the-press programme organised by the Ernakulam Press Club…
